summary: Turn 8. The Candidate from the previous turn (0069a1fe5be04660b3b91f31ac2394d4, the Accept-reply escalation gap) remains active; this turn grounds its legality premise from source instead of forming an obligation prematurely. Sourced result: a higher-ballot AcceptReply is legally reachable, because recovery raises acceptors' ballots (handlePrepare assigns inst.bal = prepare.Ballot when the prepare ballot is higher, epaxos/epaxos.go:1183-1187) and handleAccept answers a stale Accept with that higher local inst.bal while only logging 'Smaller ballot' (epaxos/epaxos.go:993-1006). So a slow-path Accept broadcast overlapping a concurrent recovery of the same instance produces Accept replies whose ballot exceeds the coordinator's lb.lastTriedBallot, and handleAcceptReply drops them at its equality guard (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026) before the unreachable greater-than block (epaxos/epaxos.go:1028-1035) — the escalation that the parallel handlePreAcceptReply path performs (nacks++ and, for a leader, makeBallot + bcastPrepare, epaxos/epaxos.go:855-870) has no counterpart on the Accept path. Submitted action=research with feedback referencing the candidate and B-ACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER / B-PREACCEPT-REPLY-LEADER / B-RECOVERY-START. The remaining discriminator is explicit and not presumed: whether the resulting non-completion is a defect or merely a bounded delay, since executeCommands re-enqueues recovery after COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, and grounding the progress duty itself rather than inferring it from the parallel handler. Also still open: IsLeader gating on non-leader coordinators, and the untouched A1 fast-path, A2 authority, A4 membership and A6 durability lines. Preflight validation returns valid=true; formal acceptance and any execution remain the controller's.
